name: Winchester
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Winchester, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Winchester, MA: Stroll Week, the Lighting of the Trees with Santa on a firetruck, and free photos with Santa downtown.
lede: Winchester turns the first week of December into Stroll Week, a run of downtown events that peaks when Santa rolls up on a firetruck for the Lighting of the Trees.
celebrates: The Winchester Chamber of Commerce runs Stroll Week, a full week of downtown events in early December. It opens with Midnight Madness shopping, then builds to the Lighting of the Trees on the Town Common, where Santa arrives by firetruck, the All School Chorus sings and the lights come on. Book Ends hosts a Polar Express storytime, A Tavola offers horse and carriage rides with dinner reservations, and kids follow a scavenger hunt and vote in a gingerbread house contest. Winchester Co-operative Bank, the lead sponsor, offers free photos with Santa on Saturday mornings.
lastyear: Stroll Week 2025, the chamber's 5th annual Holiday Stroll, ran December 1 to 7. On Friday, December 5, Santa returned to the Lighting of the Trees for the first time since before COVID, arriving by firetruck at 4:30 pm and staying until 6:30. Sogno served hot chocolate, the All School Chorus sang at 6:30 and the lights went on at 7. Olaf greeted kids for photos, and author Matt Tavares read at Book Ends.
facts: Stroll Week is young. The chamber's board came up with the idea in 2020 to bring people downtown the way Town Day and the En Ka weekends do. The gingerbread house contest, run with the Winchester Cultural District and The Gingerbread Construction Co., had its 4th year in 2025. Winchester also has one of the oldest Thanksgiving football rivalries around: in 2026 it plays Woburn for the 125th time.
trains: Winchester has two stations on the MBTA Lowell Line, Winchester Center and Wedgemere, at 25 Mystic Valley Parkway, with trains to North Station in Boston and north to Anderson/Woburn, Wilmington and Lowell. Winchester Center is close to the Town Common, so families can ride in for Stroll Week. Book Ends often reads The Polar Express during the week. For a real holiday train, Edaville in Carver runs a train through the lights, and Lowell has a streetcar museum.

kidfact: Santa does not use his sleigh in Winchester. He rides into town on a fire truck for the Lighting of the Trees.
faq: Stroll Week is the Winchester Chamber of Commerce's week of holiday events downtown in early December. It starts with Midnight Madness shopping and includes the Lighting of the Trees, storytimes, carriage rides, a scavenger hunt and a gingerbread house contest. The chamber posts the schedule on its website.
When is the Winchester tree lighting?

The Lighting of the Trees falls on the Friday of Stroll Week on the Town Common. Santa arrives by firetruck in the late afternoon, the All School Chorus sings, and the lights go on in the evening. Check this page for the current year's time and cost.
Where can kids get photos with Santa in Winchester?

Winchester Co-operative Bank at 19 Church Street offers free photos with Santa on Saturday mornings in December, with holiday treats and goodies for kids, and collects toys for its holiday toy drive. Santa also visits the Lighting of the Trees on the Town Common during Stroll Week.

Winchester has two MBTA Lowell Line stations, Winchester Center and Wedgemere. Trains run to North Station in Boston, a short ride south, and north toward Anderson/Woburn, Wilmington and Lowell. Winchester Center is the closer stop for the Town Common and Stroll Week, and Wedgemere sits on Mystic Valley Parkway.
